forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Bath and North East Somerset schools deficit reaches £46.5m, with government grant expected to cover 90%
news_drafts.lead:
Bath and North East Somerset Council's deficit on the dedicated schools grant (the government grant that funds schools) stood at £46.505m at the end of 2025/26, the council's accounts show. The in-year overspend on high needs (funding for children with special educational needs and disabilities) was £13.716m, added to £32.789m carried forward. The Department for Education has announced a High Needs Stability Grant, expected in autumn 2026 once an acceptable plan is provided, to pay 90% of the accumulated deficit. The council anticipates £41.931m, leaving £4.573m for it to fund from 2028/29.

The council's external auditor (an independent check on the accounts) says the deficit grew by 41.8% during the year and is equivalent to about 50% of usable reserves (the part of reserves the council can spend). Its auditor has identified financial sustainability as a risk of significant weakness in each audit year since 2022/23. The council has submitted a reform plan for the grant, and approval is pending. Recovery plans estimate further unmitigated deficits of £17.2m in 2026/27 and £18.8m in 2027/28. The council's own Annual Governance Statement lists the deficit and its Safety Valve Agreement with the Department for Education among two significant issues, alongside service demand and cost pressures.

A statutory override (a temporary government rule keeping such deficits off the main balance sheet) runs to 31 March 2028. The Department for Education will take over the high needs block from April 2028. The auditor's report says that if the deficits are not resolved by that date, they would have to be funded from the council's own reserves.

findings.paper_title: 9z Audit Findings Reports UPDATED & Audited Statemenet of Account 202526 Appendix 1
findings.headline: Multiple IT control deficiencies identified across financial systems
findings.detail: Audit identified: (1) new Agresso user granted roles exceeding those requested; (2) Logotech fixed asset system lacks password configuration policies; (3) Service Level Agreement with Civica payroll system provider could not be obtained for testing. Council plans to address through new Unit4 ERPx system implementation (November 2026) and migration away from Logotech.
findings.matters: IT control weaknesses increase risk of unauthorized access, data manipulation and fraud; affects confidence in segregation of duties and system controls underpinning financial reporting.
findings.quote: During the audit, it was noted that for a sample Agresso new user within the audit period, the system roles granted to the new user exceeded those requested and required for the user's role.

findings.paper_title: 9z Audit Findings Reports UPDATED & Audited Statemenet of Account 202526 Appendix 1
findings.headline: Five investment property assets identified on balance sheet that had been disposed but remained fully depreciated
findings.detail: Five investment property assets had been sold or disposed but remained on the fixed asset register as fully depreciated assets. Discovery during audit testing indicates control issue in fixed asset record-keeping. Total value of disposed assets left on register was £547k.
findings.matters: Demonstrates asset register controls are not robust; investment properties total £231.888m on balance sheet, so control gaps raise concerns about completeness and accuracy of property asset accounting.
findings.figures: £547k value of disposed assets, investment properties total £231.888m
findings.quote: As part of our consideration of depreciation we identified five Investment Property assets that were fully depreciated and remained on the fixed asset register. Further review identified that these had been sold or disposed and should have been removed. The value of these is £547k

findings.paper_title: 9z Audit Findings Reports UPDATED & Audited Statemenet of Account 202526 Appendix 1
findings.headline: £7.6m Community Infrastructure Levy and S38 contributions reclassified from short-term to long-term creditors
findings.detail: Testing identified that £7.596m of CIL and S38 payments were incorrectly classified as short-term creditors. Council could not demonstrate that accounting code criteria for short-term classification had been met (e.g., settlement within 12 months). Reclassification to long-term creditors required.
findings.matters: Proper liability classification affects working capital and creditor assessment; error indicates insufficient review of balance sheet classifications against accounting standards.
findings.quote: Management have been unable to demonstrate that these criteria have been met.

findings.paper_title: 9z Audit Findings Reports UPDATED & Audited Statemenet of Account 202526 Appendix 1
findings.headline: Journal approval process lacks formal authorization for transactions under £500k, repeat finding from prior audit
findings.detail: No formal approval process exists for journals under £500k threshold; assurance is taken from retrospective review of sample journals on monthly basis. Journals above £500k are approved but lack documented audit trail. This was also flagged in 2024/25 audit. New financial system with journal authorization process planned for November 2026.
findings.matters: Lack of formal controls over journal posting increases fraud and error risk; repeat finding suggests slow remediation; improved system will strengthen controls but interim period extends exposure.
findings.quote: As in previous years we note that no formal approval process exists for those journals under £500k and assurance is taken from review of a sample of journals, below this threshold, on a monthly basis.

findings.paper_title: 9z Audit Findings Reports UPDATED & Audited Statemenet of Account 202526 Appendix 1
findings.headline: £1.041m reclassification between Additions and REFCUS for Bath Riverside project
findings.detail: Council's allocation of Bath Riverside project expenditure between capital additions and Revenue Expenditure Financed by Capital under Statute was incorrect. Auditor recalculation identified that additions were understated by £1,041k with corresponding REFCUS overstatement due to incorrect application of the funding split ratio.
findings.matters: Accurate capital accounting affects asset reporting and revenue impact measurement; material misclassification between additions and REFCUS indicates control weakness in project accounting.
findings.quote: This is calculated on a specific ratio and recalculation of the split identified that the figures disclosed in the financial statements are incorrect. We have recalculated the split and have confirmed that additions have been understated by £1,041k and REFCUS similarly overstated by the same amount.
